procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory; registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the certificate: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice (and the factory's purchase invoice if a trading exporter), pay the fee online, submit, and print the approved certificate; processing takes about one working day.
The certificate fee is AED 50 (invoice value up to AED 100000).
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information, keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years, and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of issue.

The exporter ensures goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar, and if invoiced by a third party, the exporter must indicate third-party invoicing.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says.
De minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating.
Discrepancy between agreement and India's certificate form on box number; India's form governs entry into India.
The application must include HS code, description, quantity and value; each item must qualify separately; authority may ask for cost sheets and factory visit.
Refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources.

The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD), and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply.
